findings.recommendation: HOLD exact issuance/date and historical military-class inclusion; retain Navy instructions draft as source-supported candidate
findings.issuer_capacity: Catalog attributes Madison to Navy Secretary Crowninshield; manuscript itself is headed Instructions prepared for the Navy Dept., with no visible full signature or direct addressee. Captain Morris and frigate Congress are operational recipients in text.
findings.identity: Two-page heavily revised instructions, eight clauses; acquisition order reverses reading order. source_02 (0495d) is beginning, source_01 (0496) continuation.
operative_inventory: Proceed without delay to Gulf of Mexico and assume naval command there.
Protect commerce against piracy, distinguishing armed belligerents acting under national flags; protect against unauthorized force while preserving lawful belligerent search/laws-of-war limits.
Maintain United States territorial rights within the maritime league; aid lawful detection/suppression of smuggling.
Avoid Spanish mainland/island ports except real emergency; observe neutrality, avoid suspicious hostile appearances and unprovoked violence.
Do not use public vessels for private property, specie/bullion or passengers absent Navy Department instructions.
Do not convoy/protect belligerent vessels or vessels carrying contraband to belligerent ports.
Cooperate with United States land commanders against invasion.

quotes.text: Instructions prepared for the Navy Dept.
To communicate and co-operate, as occasion may justify & require

findings.chronology: Later bracketed image annotation reads [ca. October 19, 1816]; nearby manuscript date line appears 1815 or 16 and faint Communicated. Catalog gives Oct19 1816 without ca. Do not promote catalog precision into an unqualified signed issuance date.
limits: Interlineations/deletions require diplomatic transcription for exact operative version.
Prepared instructions evidence substantive executive work, not proof final transmission/issuance.
Military/naval content requires preserving historical exclusion/classification issue.

you are hereby authorized and directed to subdue, seize, and make prize

findings.recommendation: HOLD automatic admission; strong presidential expedition-instructions candidate with draft/version history preserved
findings.issuer_capacity: Manuscript addressed to Meriwether Lewis as Captain 1st Regiment of Infantry; final page dated June20 1803 and bears Th: Jefferson with presidential-capacity abbreviation. Body appoints Lewis to execute objects of presidential message and statute.
findings.identity: Four-page revised manuscript of expedition instructions, not merely private correspondence. Old LOC-derived embedded editorial transcription identifies [ante June20 1803] and says dateline/signature later than body circulated for comments in April.
operative_inventory: Appoint Lewis; provision equipment and attendants via War Secretary and invest him with commanding-officer powers.
Explore Missouri and Pacific-connected routes for commerce; make geographic, scientific, commercial and ethnographic observations and preserve duplicate notes.
Report observations to War Office and send periodic journals/cipher sensitive material.
Manage relations with Native peoples, visits, vaccination information and safety-driven retreat.
Provide conditional return-by-sea and credit arrangements; on safe return discharge eligible attendants, obtain pay/clothing arrears, recommend land provision, return papers to government.
Authorize written succession nominations on Lewis death, with transferred powers and further succession.

quotes.text: The object of your mission is to explore the Missouri river
Given under my hand at the city of Washington this 20th day of June 1803

findings.chronology: June20 visible manuscript date and catalog agree; ante-June20 editorial label concerns composition/version rather than necessarily contradictory issue date. April circulation note is older derivative editorial evidence, not independently inspected April correspondence.
limits: Image signature/date support authorship/capacity, not complete issuance transmission chain or original autograph authentication.
Military command, scientific expedition, administrative directions and letter form require explicit historical-class treatment; no silent admission under proposed supplement.

findings.recommendation: HOLD final instrument/version/issuance and historical military-class inclusion; keep bundle components distinct
findings.issuer_capacity: Catalog Jefferson to Wilkinson; initial text refers to Executive and instructs Genl Wilkinson. Seven images include heavily revised instructions, multiple convention heads/variants and envelope addressed The President of the U States, Washington. No completed outward signed letter established.
findings.identity: Composite drafting bundle. 1148 begins Nov8 1806 Represent to Genl Wilkinson; 1149/1150 contain parallel versions Heads of a Convention; 1151 substitute first article/notes; 1152 insertion marked (a); 1153 further alternatives; 1154 envelope. One catalog row is not one proven issuance.
operative_inventory: Explain desire to avoid actual hostilities, temporary Sabine separation, and Bayou Pierre position.
Direct Wilkinson to propose written convention to Spanish commandant; conditional withdrawal to Fort Adams with residual force at Natchitoches; defensive posture if no convention.

Proposed convention: suspension of hostilities/separation line, alternative clauses on cross-border intercourse, military establishments, Native peoples neutrality/self-government, prisoner release, ratification/revocation terms.

Alternative insertion: agree temporary line; conditional evacuation of Bayou Pierre; defense without crossing Sabine; conditional Spanish-post evacuation east of Mississippi with New Orleans safety exception and absolute east-of-Pearl limit.

quotes.text: Nov. 8. 1806. Represent to Genl Wilkinson
Heads of a Convention to be proposed
you must not, in any event whatever, cross the Sabine river
The President of the U States

findings.chronology: Nov8 1806 on initial page and one convention version agrees catalog. No image establishes dates of all edits, their order, or final dispatched wording.
limits: Do not treat draft alternatives as simultaneously enacted provisions.
No proof convention concluded or conditional military movements occurred.
Envelope direction prevents simplistic assumption every page is Jefferson outward instruction; precise contributor/hand allocation remains unresolved.

findings.issuer_capacity: Catalog Polk; draft addresses House of Representatives as presidential response. Not addressed to Slidell. No executed signed message copy authenticated here.
findings.identity: 0795 cover explicitly rough draft of part of message refusing communication of instructions; 0805 cover calls rough sheets of first draft of message to House, revised and copied before sent. operative_inventory: Proposed response transmits departmental reports and selected correspondence while declining disclosure of Slidell instructions because ongoing/resumable negotiations and public interest.

quotes.text: Rough Draft of part of Message, refusing to communicate
Instructions to Mr Slidell, Minister to Mexico
To the House of Representatives
Revised & copied before sent in.

findings.chronology: Catalog Jan12 1848 and cover bracket date concern message drafting. References to prior ministerial instructions, Washington1796, annual message December8 1846 and naval instruction of May13 1846 do not establish new 1848 instrument issuances.

findings.issuer_capacity: mjm017456 corrected manuscript ends James Madison, Aug13 1814. mjm022917 starts (Copy), also dated Aug13 and ends James Madison; docket to General Armstrong. Official Department of War relations/procedure, not private personal correspondence on these pages.
findings.identity: mjm017456 three image files comprise four manuscript sides: reading order page03, page01 left, page01 right, page02. mjm022917 copy is ms pp125–130 plus blank/docket: local page08 then01–05,06 blank,07 docket. Same heading, opening, ten reporting categories, emergency exception, closing and date independently observed.
operative_inventory: Require prior presidential communication of ten listed War Department actions: general/permanent regulations; courts on generals; appointments beyond routine uncontested promotions; dismissals; consolidations/transfers; senior resignations; militia calls/receipts; treaty instructions; military movements instructions; district/command changes.
Permit urgent waiver while President absent, with subsequent communication without delay.
Immediately communicate military intelligence and other matters intended/proper for presidential knowledge.

quotes.text: The following course will be observed in future
(Copy)
In the absence of the President from the seat of Government
August 13. 1814

findings.chronology: Both image sets carry Aug13 1814; identity conclusion rests on copied substantive sequence and explicit Copy, not date alone.
limits: Copied signature does not authenticate an autograph. Exact word-level diplomatic equivalence not asserted across deleted draft text and fair copy.
Retain distinct document/version IDs; cluster issuance hypothesis rather than count each LOC item.
Administrative oversight of military department differs from direct field command but historical inclusion still requires explicit adjudication.
